_note: The HUD's few gameplay numbers (ours). Plates: an enemy's name and bars show only after you have damaged them, for `afterHit` seconds from the last hit, and only while the line from your eye to their chest is clear of the level; a team mate's always. A plate is last drawn at `range` metres, fading from `fadeFrom`: the owner asked for them off far away as well as behind cover, so this is a room-and-a-half, not the width of the map.
_loot: Looting, so that kitting up after a landing is not dozens of presses with your head down (ours; Apex, Warzone and The Finals all take ammo as you walk over it and let you hold one key to empty a box). `reach` is the radius round your feet the prompt's list covers, wider than loot.json's 2.2 m aimed reach so a whole spot fits in one list, and `floorGap` keeps that list to the floor you are standing on now that the buildings hold loot upstairs. `sweep` is the walk-over radius: an item whose kind is in `autoKinds` and, for a heal, whose id is in `autoHeals`, comes up inside it with no press at all. `startAfter` is how long the key must stay down before the hold starts emptying the spot, so a tap still takes exactly one thing; `cadence` is the gap between the ones after that, slow enough to read the notices and fast enough to clear a death box in a second. `askAgain` stops a guest asking the host for the same item every frame while the answer is still in flight. `listMax` is how many rows the list shows, and `cycle` is the action that steps it: the armour cycle, a range tool with nothing to do in a battle royale, so it is free to borrow here.
_swapGuard: loot.swapGuard: seconds after you take a gun during which a gun that appears within reach is left out of the list. Taking a gun with both slots full puts the one in hand down at your feet, inside the reach list, and nearest. A press read over several frames, or a hold, took it straight back and put the new one down, and the two swapped every frame for as long as the key was down. Ours: long enough to cover a press and let go, short enough that a gun dropped by someone else a moment later is still offered.
_boxClear: loot.boxClear: metres round a death box inside which the walk-over pickup takes nothing. A box's things are spread 0.9 m round it (brmatch.ts dropBox), so 1.6 covers them with a margin. Without it a squad mate respawning the owner at the box swept up the ammo and heals the owner was meant to get back. Ours.
_damageDir: Where you are being shot from: a red arc round the crosshair pointing at whoever hit you, the way Apex, Warzone and every other shooter since Halo draws it. Without it a hit from behind was a number going down and no idea which way to turn. life is how long an arc lasts after the last hit from that direction, radius and thick its size in HUD pixels at 1080p, arc its width in degrees. A new hit from within merge metres of an arc's source refreshes that arc instead of stacking a second one, and at most max are shown, newest first. Ours.
_reticle: The crosshair's options (Settings, Crosshair; src/game/reticle.ts). The default is the crosshair the game always had, Apex's three prongs and a dot, white, dynamic with the gun's spread, so nobody sees a change until they ask for one. The colours are the ones every competitive shooter offers, and they are chosen to stay apart for the three common kinds of colour blindness: the green and the magenta, and the yellow and the cyan, are the pairs to use when red and green look alike. limits are the ranges the settings accept; a stored value outside them is clamped. Ours.
_summary: The match summary: the card over the middle of the screen when a match ends, with the result, your numbers, the XP it paid and the level bar filling. show is how long it stays, seconds; fill is how long the level bar takes to run from where you were to where you are, which is the moment the XP reads as earned rather than as a number. A new match starting takes it down at once. Ours.
_accessibility: Settings, Accessibility (src/game/palette.ts). vision is the set of meaning colours per kind of colour vision: enemy and ally, the softer pair the kill feed uses for its lines, and the damage arcs as r,g,b. Red against green is the pair about one man in twelve cannot tell apart, so the two red-green modes move the enemy to orange and your side to blue, and the blue-yellow mode keeps red but moves your side to a teal that stays clear of it. The normal set is the colours the HUD always used. scales are the HUD sizes offered; a free number is not accepted, because a HUD scaled to 4 is off the screen. Ours, after the palettes Valorant, Apex and Fortnite ship.
_quickChat: Quick chat: the chat key opens these lines and 1 to 6 sends one to everyone in the match, where it shows in the kill feed with your name. A browser game has no text chat worth the name while you are aiming, and playing with a friend with no way to say GG or wait was the gap. open is how long the list stays up untouched, seconds; gap is the least time between two lines, so a key held down or mashed is not a flood. A line travels as its number, so a guest's text never reaches anyone: nobody can type into anyone else's screen. Ours.
_loading: The loading screen (src/ui/loading.ts): up for at least minSeconds so it does not flash, gone once everything asked for is in and a frame is drawn, or after maxSeconds whatever happens. With nothing asked for at all (a page served from the cache) it goes after quietSeconds. A tip turns over every tipSeconds. Ours.

tips: Look straight down in the drop to dive fast, level to glide far.
In a squad the host is the jumpmaster. Press C to break off and fly yourself.
A Ring Console shows your whole squad where the ring goes after next.
Resurgence: every kill by your side takes 5 s off a dead squad mate's wait.
Hold the interact key over a pile of loot to take everything at your feet.
Crouch while you sprint to slide, and jump out of the slide to keep its speed.
M opens the map. The middle mouse button pings a place, an item or an enemy for your squad.
The Mast at the hub is seven floors to the best loot on the map, and everyone knows it.
Walk into a place and its name comes up. The quieter corners are walled compounds.
